tldr: Alibaba announced Qwen4-Max general access after a preview, while Governor Barr outlined financial-stability and agent-authorization concerns in a November 16 speech; publisher claims and official views are attributed.

Catch-up coverage includes Meituan's November 15 audio-driven avatar release and Microsoft's November 10 dormant-neuron backdoor research; two technology and two terminology proposals remain under review.

news.title: Alibaba formally releases Qwen4-Max after its November 11 preview
news.summary: Alibaba announced general access to Qwen4-Max, a 2.4-trillion-total-parameter sparse MoE activating 71 billion per token, with native vision and a one-million-token context window. The company describes cybersecurity training filters and CBRN safeguards alongside QwenCloud and Alibaba platform access.
news.why_it_matters: Updates the earlier preview with a production-facing named endpoint and concrete model architecture, creating a materially changed option for large-context API users.
news.caveat: The 60% average cost-per-task improvement, Work360 rankings, software-security results and scientific demonstrations are Alibaba's own claims, not independent replications. The flagship is API/app-accessible; smaller open-weight Qwen4 models are promised, not yet verified as available.

news.title: Meituan publishes LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.6 with audio-driven long-form video
news.summary: Meituan's November 15 announcement and public Hugging Face card describe an MIT-labeled audio-conditioned avatar generator with improvements to lip synchronization, facial/body motion and autoregressive video continuation. Its examples cover single- and multi-character generation, LoRA-adapter mixing and optional reduced-precision inference.
news.why_it_matters: A downloadable reference implementation for studying speech-conditioned character animation, including extended videos and inference tradeoffs.
news.caveat: Ten-minute-plus stability and preference rankings are publisher-reported. Demonstration examples use two CUDA GPUs; hardware minimum, full practical throughput, downstream dependencies and consent/deepfake misuse controls require evaluation.

news.title: Federal Reserve governor warns of financial-stability risks from AI agents and infrastructure debt
news.summary: In a November 16 speech, Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr highlighted advanced-computing debt and opaque financing, correlated AI trading strategies, autonomous-agent account authorization, cybersecurity risks and consumer lending fairness.
news.why_it_matters: Connects AI infrastructure investment and agent deployment to specific financial-system failure modes and requirements for authorization, oversight, explainability and reproducibility.
news.caveat: These are the governor's risk assessments and scenarios, not a new Federal Reserve regulation, proof of systemic failure, or official consensus of the Board. The November 13 Financial Stability Report was already cataloged and is not a new event.

news.title: Microsoft researchers demonstrate a weight-editing backdoor against tool-using agents
news.summary: Microsoft researchers disclosed Lazarus, a controlled demonstration in which small edits to dormant model neurons create trigger-dependent malicious output while ordinary behavior can appear unchanged. Their paper reports tests on several models and early detection results.
news.why_it_matters: Adds weight integrity and trusted checkpoint provenance to agent threat models, beyond filtering prompts and testing ordinary model outputs.
news.caveat: This is a controlled research attack, not evidence that the technique is circulating in the wild. Detection figures are study-specific and do not establish guaranteed checkpoint safety; do not infer that every model is vulnerable.
